Shizuku needs to access local network. It is controlled by the network permission.

Some systems (such as MIUI) disallow apps to access the network when they are not visible, even if the app uses foreground service as standard. Please disable battery optimization features for Shizuku on such systems.

In addition, Shizuku can be started automatically on boot. If not, please check if your system or third-party tools have restricted Shizuku.

Your device manufacturer has restricted adb permissions and apps using Shizuku will not work properly.

Usually, this limitation can be lifted by adjusting some options in "Developer options". Please read the help for details on how to do this.

You may need to restart Shizuku for the operation to take effect.
The permission of adb is limited

It\'s highly possible that your device manufacturer limits the permission of adb.

There may be a solution for your system in this document.
Run commands through Shizuku in terminal apps you like
First, Export files to any where you want. You will find two files, %1$s and %2$s.

If there are files with the same name in the selected folder, they will be deleted.\n\nThe export function uses SAF (Storage Access Framework). It\'s reported that MIUI breaks the functions of SAF. If you are using MIUI, you may have to extract the file from Shizuku\'s apk or download from GitHub.
Then, use any text editor to open and edit %1$s.
For example, if you want to use Shizuku in %1$s, you should replace %2$s with %3$s (%4$s is the package name of %1$s).
Finally, move the files to somewhere where your terminal app can access, you will be able to use %1$s to run commands through Shizuku.
Some tips: grant execute permission to %1$s and add it to %2$s, you will able to use %1$s directly.

With %1$s, in any terminal app, you can connect to and interact with the shell runs by Shizuku.

Complete guide for Wireless Debugging activation & managing Android/data and obb files without root.

1. Enable Developer Options:
Go to Phone Settings → About Phone → Tap Build Number 7 times until you are a developer.

2. Enable Wireless Debugging:
Go to System / Additional Settings → Developer Options, and turn ON Wireless Debugging while connected to Wi-Fi.
IMPORTANT: Realme / Oppo / OnePlus / Xiaomi Users

Realme, Oppo, OnePlus, and Xiaomi systems block ADB communication by default.

You MUST enable this setting in Developer Options:
• Realme / Oppo / OnePlus: Find and turn ON \"Disable permission monitoring\".
• Xiaomi / HyperOS / MIUI: Turn ON \"USB debugging (Security settings)\".

If not enabled, the app will get stuck at \"Waiting for service\".

1. Tap the Pair button in this app.
2. A search notification will appear in your notification panel.
3. Go to Developer Options → Wireless Debugging → Pair device with pairing code.
4. Enter the 6-digit code in Shizuku\'s notification and press Send.
5. The notification will confirm \"Pairing successful\".

* Pairing only needs to be done once per Wi-Fi network.

1. Return to the home screen of this app.
2. Tap the Start button under Wireless Debugging card.
3. The terminal will start Shizuku server and automatically close once completed.
4. The status on the home screen will change to Running / Active.

* If you reboot your device in the future, you do NOT need to pair again. Just enable Wireless Debugging and tap Start.

Once Shizuku is running:
1. Tap the Data & OBB Explorer card on the home screen.
2. Browse game and app data / obb directories directly.
3. Use the toolbar actions to create New Folder, New File, Delete, or Copy Files freely.

Q: Why is it stuck on \"Waiting for service\"?
A: Make sure you have enabled \"Disable permission monitoring\" in Developer Options.

Q: Why is status \"Not running\" after restarting phone?
A: Android shuts down ADB processes when rebooting. Simply turn on Wireless Debugging in Settings and tap Start in Shizuku.

Q: Top-right Reload Icon:
A: Checks whether the server and wireless debugging port are currently active.
